title: Research: one-sided residue closures — Circuit Lemma, relative root counting and plane lemma close 480 of the 603 d>=4 residues (116 open; no kappa claim)
body:
Follow-up to #2816, #2826, #2862 and `research/one-sided-excess-three` (all ours). Adds only `research/one-sided-residue-closures/`; nothing existing is changed. **No kappa claim, no window, no supplier word.**

## What is shown

For the lift `S ⊇ 𝒞(E8)` of a one-sided P112 decoder, the weight multisets `(d, w)` of the minimum basis of `T = (ρS)_{≤7}` with `d >= 4` and slack `cost(T) - 8d <= 7` are a list of 603 residue cells. For each closed cell, `cost_w(S) >= 72`.

* **Class I** (PROVEN): slack 7 forces `x = c_8 = z = D = 0`, so the pieces are basis members with drop 0. The slack-6 scenarios (extra line, one heavier piece, one 7 missing) are treated as separate variants that must all die.
* **Circuit Lemma**, T-level and E8 version (PROVEN): for `|K| <= d-1` there is `c != 0` in `R` vanishing on `K`, and `Off_E(h(c))` lies in the union of the remaining flats.
* **Relative root counting** (PROVEN): with `|K0| = d-j`, more than `N_j` root directions of `cap <= 77` with pairwise `cap <= 56` cannot sit in a `j`-space. `N_2, N_3` (and `N_4` with `FULL=1`) are exhaustive; `N_5, N_6` come from the ADE classification. The audit's fix is included: the base configuration is now tested in every `s = 6` variant (no result changes).
* **Lemma P** (plane lemma L1/L2) and **Lemma P'** (weighted count) (PROVEN), now applied at T-level to all 603 rows (375 kills, 125 of them by L1 alone, no covering data needed). The covering facts behind the parameters are recomputed by `cov.c`. **Fact D corrected:** "no `Off` has 89-91 lines" is false (3584 directions with `|Off| = 89`); harmless, since four 6-flats cannot cover 80 of those 89 lines.
* **Consolidated ledger** of every row: **480 KILLED** by audited sources, **7 KILLED(prior-only)**, **116 OPEN**. The 7 (all `d = 8`) rest on one earlier single-implementation `(6,6,5)` span run at target 7 that was not re-audited; without it 123 rows are open. Open rows by `(d, slack)`: (4,7) 2; (6,7) 11; (7,6) 11; (7,7) 17; (8,5) 11; (8,6) 24; (8,7) 40. A further 56 rows are closed by additional single-implementation span runs that are not included here; they will follow once independently re-checked.

The 603-row input list comes from the earlier enumeration and is not re-derived here.

## Checks

`bash verify.sh` (about 6 minutes, at most 3 busy processes, `timeout` on every process; needs numpy and a C compiler): manifest; constants (`g(1..8)`, `N_2`, `N_3`); the frame stabiliser (order 172,032, label-linear) and the complete direction list `|Off| <= 89` (21,340 non-E8 masks in 17 orbits); exact coverings (root target and the `|Off| = 79, 80` targets recomputed and compared, the other 15 shipped as recorded outputs); covering facts mapped to the parameters of Lemma P; the D7 plane fact; every RRC certificate re-verified; the whole ledger recomputed and compared byte for byte with `data/ledger_consolidated.csv`. `FULL=1` recomputes all 17 coverings and the exhaustive `N_4` (about 56 more CPU-minutes). `evidence/` holds the timing logs of the full covering runs and a default run's output.

Credit: Lemma B and the kill criterion of #2826 / `one-sided-excess-three`, the notation and peeling of #2816, the decoder-floor notes `one-sided-decoders-all-m` and `one-sided-six-multisets`.
